Cable bore or solid blanking plug, moulded from the same groove geometry. One panel hole, two parts — useful when a variant deletes an option and the hole stays.
It has to grip on a cold morning
Rubber stiffens as it cools, and a grommet held only by grip is most likely to let go at −20 °C. EPDM is our default here for that reason, not just for weather.

Dimensioned drawings and 3D models are issued on request, under NDA where required. Send the panel gauge, the hole diameter and the cable size — or a sample with a panel offcut — and we will return a drawing for approval.
What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes — and send a piece of the panel with the sample. A grommet that has been in service has relaxed and measures loose; the panel does not change. We take the groove from the panel gauge and the bore from your cable size.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?

PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP. Mark the finished panel thickness, the panel hole diameter, the cable size and the push-out force you need — those four, plus the compound, are enough for us to quote and tool.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412, compression set to ASTM D395 Method B and tear strength to ASTM D624 are tested in-house, and push-out force is verified on first article.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?
TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment.
